text:
olivia: Heads-up: ran into a nasty runtime error when deploying the sample-app to Cloudflare Workers using Vite + worker adapter. Looks bundler-specific and related to mixed ESM/CJS in the SDK.

ben: paste the error? which SDK package exactly?

olivia: `redwood-inference-js@0.12.3` from our registry. Error at runtime: 
```
ReferenceError: exports is not defined
  at f (/assets/index.js:1:234)
  at handleRequest (edge-runtime:56)
```
This only shows up in the deployed worker; local `vite dev` and Node SSR are fine.

harry: that smells like an IIFE-wrapped CJS chunk shipped into an ESM worker bundle. Can you share your Vite build output or the problematic bundle snippet?

olivia: minimal repro steps I used:
1) `npm init -y && npm i vite@4 @cloudflare/workers-types redwood-inference-js`
2) index.mjs:
```js
import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference-js';
export default {
  fetch() {
    const c = createClient({ apiKey: 'x' });
    return new Response('ok');
  }
}
```
3) `vite build --ssr` then `wrangler publish --target=modules`

olivia: when I inspect `dist/assets/index.js` there is a small IIFE that references `exports` even though the bundle is ESM. That breaks under the worker runtime.

ben: FYI rollup + some babel setups can convert `export default` into `exports.default` patterns. If the SDK ships a `.mjs` that was generated from a CJS pipeline, some bundlers won't tree-shake the interop helpers.

harry: Workarounds that worked for me in two customers' repos:
- Vite: set `ssr.noExternal: ['redwood-inference-js']` and `optimizeDeps.include` to force ESM processing.
- Rollup: add a plugin to replace `exports.` with `export ` in the SDK files (hacky).
- Webpack: add rule to transpile the SDK through Babel so the interop helpers are normalized.

ben: we should not recommend hacks. Action items: (1) SDK team to publish a pure ESM build that has no CJS interop helper calls in the `.mjs` entry; (2) update package.json `exports` to have clear `import`/`require` targets; (3) ship types via `types` field and include `.d.ts`.

olivia: also saw TypeScript users hit `any` issues because `types` wasn't resolving when bundlers externalized the package. Adding `types` at top-level helped in my repro.

harry: I'll create a small CI job that runs builds for Vite/Rollup/Webpack with the sample-app and fails if the bundle contains "exports." in an ESM file. That should catch regressions.

ci-bot: CI: sample-app-workers build #342 failed earlier, logs: https://ci.internal/342/logs (contains failing bundle sample)

ben: Great. Olivia, can you PR a tiny repro repo (single file + package.json + vite config) to the sdk/internal-repros repo? Put a README with the exact steps and the failing bundle snippet. We'll link it to the SDK issue.

olivia: done, PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-internal-repros/pull/12 (includes worker repro and a note about edge runtime limits).

harry: I'll draft the SDK packaging PR: expose `./dist/index.mjs` as import-only and `./dist/index.cjs` as require, ensure rollup output avoids `interopHelpers: true` or strip them.

olivia: for docs, can we add a short "Edge bundlers" DX note listing `ssr.noExternal` as a temporary fix and recommend `pure ESM` from SDK long-term? saves customers time.

ben: agreed. I'll add a short doc snippet in the SDK repo under `docs/dx/edge-bundlers.md`.

olivia: thanks all. marking this thread as resolved once packaging PR is merged. :white_check_mark:
